hints.title: Ancestor Range Constraint
hints.text: Comparing a node only to its immediate left and right children is insufficient because all descendants in the left subtree must be smaller than every ancestor. How can you propagate allowable value boundaries downward?

hints.title: Narrowing Interval Invariant
hints.text: Every node in a valid search tree must satisfy a strict range low < val < high, which narrows as you traverse down each branch.

hints.title: Recursive Range Propagation Procedure
hints.text: Define a helper function taking a node, low bound, and high bound, initialized to negative and positive infinity. If the node is null, return true. If node.val <= low or node.val >= high, return false. Recursively validate left with (low, node.val) and right with (node.val, high).

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: number of nodes in tree (1 <= N <= 10^4)
H: tree height (log N balanced, N skewed)
complexity.notes: Single pass checking each node against its inherited upper and lower bounds.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Checking only immediate children (e.g. node.left.val < node.val < node.right.val) fails on trees like [5, 1, 4, null, null, 3, 6] where 3 is in the right subtree of 5.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Propagating upper and lower bounds checks each node once in O(N) time and O(H) auxiliary space without building an auxiliary array.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Using open intervals (strict inequalities), handling 32-bit integer boundary values (e.g. INT_MIN and INT_MAX) using infinity or 64-bit bounds, and understanding alternative in-order traversal approach.

solutions.approach: Upper and Lower Bound Interval Propagation
